placements.title: a prior failure crystallizes into a mandatory, owned deployment control
placements.frame: Does the control here exist because a concrete incident forced it into being — and is it performed as already settled rather than argued for?
placements.why: Both segments perform the same theme: Quinton's declarative (src-1) enacts the gate as already in force with its justification closed by a prior incident ('that is the whole reason for the gate'), and the summary (src-2) codifies the same gate as a ratified decision with scope and owner. The theme — how a concrete failure becomes a non-negotiable, owned deployment control — is a narrative subject future envelopes will keep feeding as other gates, controls, or incident-driven mandates accrue. The directional observations converge across affect, register, relational, power, value, and conviction on this single thematic read.
